_help.about: (§CN blocks wired, design §CN) Delves (design §CJ): the underground of the ruins. Room counts, finds and log lines still live in code (Delves, RuinBuilder) and can move here when Claude Code next touches them (PROGRESS 2 Oct asked for this file). This first version holds §CN's fire-holders and overrun dens. Restart after editing.
_help.fire_holders: Every delve room except the stairs (skip) has one old, cold fire-holder (per_room). The first room's is its existing old hearth (first_room, OldHearths, as built). The others suit the ruin (by_ruin; default when the kind isn't listed): a hearth ring, a brazier in a castle's undercroft, a wall sconce in a tower. The heart holds the ash of the last fire (heart; §CJ.7). They start cold and empty (start_units 0): each must be laid (fuel.json kindling: kindling, then fuel) and lit with the torch's swing (torch.json swing). Lit, it is a fire like any other for its fuel (holds_units at most): a fire's radius nothing enters (§BA), light_radius_m. First guesses. (design §CO) nest_den: a cave mouth's or grotto's den is only the small chamber behind the mouth until Phase 3 digs the caves beyond, so its fire is the hearth at the opening (fire: opening_hearth), and lighting it clears the den (clears). When real caves are dug, a deep cave is cleared at its heart, like a barrow (deep_caves_later).
_help.overrun: An overrun delve (camps.json sim.overrun). Below, it is always night (below_always_night): what holds it is there whatever the hour. The biome's hunter (dread.json hunters) holds hunter_share of overrun delves; the rest are the biome's night roster (§CH; at an ordinary den the hunter is rare). At night they also come up: within night_surface.radius_m of the ruin, outside a fire's radius, dread fills dread_scale times as fast; by day the surface is quiet. tells: what gives it away, read in the world (no UI). When the heart's fire is lit, whatever held it leaves by the delve's way out (§CJ.4). First guesses.

log.heart_lit: The fire at the heart caught. Whatever held this place has gone.
log.settled: Folk have come to the fire.
